h: Making a West London Day of It
p: A trampoline session is short and sweet by design, usually an hour or so of full-throttle bouncing, which means you'll have plenty of the day left to fill. Luckily, Acton sits in a part of West London with some brilliant follow-ups within a short hop.

Kew Gardens is the big one: a world-famous botanic garden with glasshouses, treetop walkway and acres to roam. It's a lovely way to calm everyone down after the noise and energy of the trampolines. Over in Brentford, the London Museum of Water and Steam is a great find for curious kids, with enormous Victorian pumping engines, and The Musical Museum nearby is packed with self-playing instruments and a mighty theatre organ.
Ealing's Walpole Park, home to Pitzhanger Manor, the house designed by the architect Sir John Soane, is a peaceful green spot with a playground and a café.

A few tips to get the most out of your bounce. Most trampoline parks ask for a waiver form to be filled in before you jump, and doing it online before you leave home saves a queue at the desk. Bring a water bottle, because bouncing is thirsty work, and give everyone a light snack beforehand rather than a big meal.
If you've got a toddler and an older child, look out for sessions aimed at little ones, which tend to be calmer, and don't be afraid to ask the staff for advice on which slot suits your group.
It's also worth keeping in mind that school holiday afternoons are the busiest times, so an earlier session can be more relaxed.
